text:
Mike: Heads-up — noticed a p95 regression in paged-attn after the hybrid-slab allocator rollout this morning. Patch rolled at 09:12 and p95 for long-context (4096) requests jumped ~18% on flashv2-batched.
Tara: ugh. numbers?
Mike: quick grab from prod telemetry: model=flashv2-batched, seq=4096, p50=42ms -> 44ms (ok), p95=210ms -> 248ms (regression), kv-page-miss-rate 3.2% -> 9.1%, block-table-frag 14% -> 33%.
Cheng: sounds like more frequent KV paging (misses) is driving stalls. Any correlation with batch sizing changes?
Mike: we also shipped the new continuous-batcher tweak (threshold from 8ms -> 5ms) at same time. Batching density went up slightly but tail worsened.
Eli: infra-bot shows deploy event: infra-bot: deploy hybrid-slab-alloc v2 -> production @2365412100 by @sam
Sam: I pushed both allocator and batcher commits in same PR to reduce rollout churn, sorry. I can roll back one. My local benchmarks didn't show p95 regression for 4096, only microbench.
Tara: can we repro in staging? If KV miss rate spikes, that suggests allocation pattern caused page scattering and extra NVMe reads for paged-attn.
Mike: repro steps I used (staging):
```
rbw bench --model flashv2-batched --seq 4096 --concurrency 16 --duration 120s --workload paged-attn --kv-pop 0.7
```
produces p95 ~240ms and sampler shows recurring page faults at ~30s intervals.
Cheng: screenshot of flame/trace: https://internal.redwood/infradb/traces/trace-2365412345 (flame shows spikes in kv_pager::evict + paged_attn::page_wait)
Sam: looking at allocator metrics, hybrid-slab introduced smaller free chunks in pagehouse arenas which increased fragmentation under long-lived KV resident sets.
Eli: could be the block-table growth policy too — we recently changed block-table.handoff to lazy-grow; that plus fragmentation = more frequent compaction which blocks paged-attn paths.
Cheng: proposal: temporarily prefer fused-attn kernel for seq>=2048 in kernel-selector (more tolerant to page latency) and lower batcher aggressiveness for requests that hit paged-KV heavy paths.
Tara: +1. Also try reducing kv-pager.target_fill_ratio from 0.7 -> 0.55 and enable a short compaction throttle so compaction doesn't run in hotspot threads.
Mike: I can test three things in staging in parallel:
- revert continuous-batcher threshold to 8ms
- set kernel-selector: prefer fused-attn for seq>=2048
- kv pager tweak target_fill_ratio=0.55 + compaction_throttle_ms=50
Cheng: run them individually and capture profiler. If we revert batcher and p95 goes back -> batcher is culprit; if kernel change helps -> kernel sensitivity to page latency matters.
Sam: I'll prepare a quick canary patch for kernel-selector and kv-pager config. Will tag you all. If that helps, we can roll to prod in 2-stage deploy.
Eli: any microbench evidence on fused vs flashv2 for 4k workloads under simulated page latency?
Mike: yes I ran a small sim with induced 2ms page read latency (local fuzzer). Results:
- flashv2-batched: p95 260ms (+heavy tail)
- fused-attn: p95 195ms (more stable, slightly higher p50)
So fused is more robust to paging noise.
Tara: ok action items:
- Mike: run the three staging runs and post perf diffs (by EOD)
- Sam: prepare canary for kernel-selector + kv-pager config (PR + smoke) — target tomorrow morning
- Cheng: add a perf test that injects page read latency into CI for paged-attn smoke
- Eli: open an infra ticket to track allocator fragmentation (attach allocator stack traces and arenas stats)
Sam: noted. I'll also add a temporary metric: pager.page_read_latency_histogram tagged by allocator_version.
Mike: created ticket RED-ENG-3417 for the regression with initial notes + links to trace.
infra-bot: RED-ENG-3417 created by Mike and assigned to Sam (link: https://pm.redwood/RED-ENG-3417)
Cheng: if staging repro fails, we still should throttle compaction/unblock hot threads as a safe fallback.
Tara: thanks everyone. Keep updates in this thread — if staging confirms a single root cause we can fast-track rollback for that component.
Sam: will ping once canary is up.
Mike: thanks — also dropping this quick kernel decision heuristic we can try in kernel-selector config:
```
# kernel-selector snippet
- if sequence_length >= 2048 and kv_pager.miss_rate > 0.01: prefer = fused-attn
- else if sequence_length <= 2048 and model.supports_flashv2: prefer = flashv2-batched
- fallback: fused-attn
```
Eli: looks good. Add a guard to log when selector overrides model-optimal kernel so we can measure impact.
Sam: rolling canary now, will report.
Mike: (added :eyes: reaction)
